title: Fast Wildfire Forces 16,000 to Leave Homes in Southern California
summaryZh: 南加州橘郡野火延燒約570英畝，至少6棟房屋受損，約1.6萬人撤離。
summaryHi: दक्षिणी कैलिफ़ोर्निया में तेज़ जंगल की आग से कम से कम 6 घर क्षतिग्रस्त, लगभग 16,000 लोग हटाए गए।

summaryEn: A fast wildfire in Orange County damaged at least six homes and forced about 16,000 people to leave.
paragraphs: A fast-moving wildfire on the Orange County coast in Southern California damaged or destroyed at least six homes and forced around 16,000 residents to evacuate, before firefighters began to gain the upper hand over the weekend.

The Norte Fire broke out on Friday morning near San Clemente and spread towards the wealthy city of San Juan Capistrano. Powerful Santa Ana winds, which blow from inland towards the sea, drove the flames across dry hillsides and into neighbourhoods, while unusually high temperatures and low humidity added to the danger. The fire eventually covered about 570 acres.

Hundreds of firefighters attacked the blaze from the ground and the air. Two were taken to hospital with heat-related injuries. Interstate 5, the main highway linking Orange County and San Diego, was temporarily shut in both directions, and emergency shelters were opened.

By Saturday, crews had achieved 25% containment and most evacuation orders had been lifted, although restrictions remained on one street in San Clemente. California also secured federal funding from FEMA to help cover firefighting costs.

The Norte Fire was one of several blazes during a period of high fire risk. A separate fire burned more than 3,000 acres at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton. The cause of the Norte Fire is still under investigation.
A big fire started on Friday in Orange County, in southern California. It started near the town of San Clemente and moved to San Juan Capistrano.
Strong, hot winds pushed the fire fast. The weather was very hot and very dry. About 16,000 people had to leave their homes.
The fire burned about 570 acres. It damaged or destroyed at least six big homes near the sea. Two firefighters were hurt by the heat.
Hundreds of firefighters worked on the ground and in the air. Helicopters dropped water on the fire. A big road, Interstate 5, was closed for some time.
By Saturday, most people could go back home. Nobody knows yet how the fire started.
A fast-moving wildfire in Southern California damaged or destroyed at least six homes and forced about 16,000 people to leave their communities on the Orange County coast.

The Norte Fire started on Friday morning near San Clemente and spread towards San Juan Capistrano. Strong Santa Ana winds, very high temperatures and dry plants helped the flames move quickly across the hills and into neighbourhoods. The fire grew to about 570 acres.

Hundreds of firefighters fought the fire from the ground and the air, with helicopters dropping water. Two firefighters were taken to hospital because of the heat. Interstate 5, the main road between Orange County and San Diego, was closed in both directions for a time.
By Saturday, firefighters had controlled 25% of the fire, and most evacuation orders were lifted. Shelters opened in San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano, and some schools closed early.
Other fires were also burning in the region, including a bigger one at the Camp Pendleton military base. Officials say the cause of the Norte Fire is still being investigated.

A fast-moving wildfire on the Orange County coast in Southern California damaged or destroyed at least six homes and forced around 16,000 residents to evacuate, before firefighters began to gain the upper hand over the weekend.

The Norte Fire broke out on Friday morning near San Clemente and spread towards the wealthy city of San Juan Capistrano. Powerful Santa Ana winds, which blow from inland towards the sea, drove the flames across dry hillsides and into neighbourhoods, while unusually high temperatures and low humidity added to the danger. The fire eventually covered about 570 acres.

Hundreds of firefighters attacked the blaze from the ground and the air. Two were taken to hospital with heat-related injuries. Interstate 5, the main highway linking Orange County and San Diego, was temporarily shut in both directions, and emergency shelters were opened.

By Saturday, crews had achieved 25% containment and most evacuation orders had been lifted, although restrictions remained on one street in San Clemente. California also secured federal funding from FEMA to help cover firefighting costs.

The Norte Fire was one of several blazes during a period of high fire risk. A separate fire burned more than 3,000 acres at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton. The cause of the Norte Fire is still under investigation.

A wind-driven wildfire tore through coastal Orange County in Southern California late last week, damaging or destroying at least six homes and prompting evacuation orders affecting roughly 16,000 residents.

The Norte Fire ignited on Friday morning near San Clemente and advanced rapidly towards the affluent city of San Juan Capistrano. Fierce Santa Ana winds, which sweep from the interior towards the coast, propelled the flames across parched hillsides and into residential streets, while unseasonable heat and low humidity compounded the threat. The blaze ultimately scorched around 570 acres.

Hundreds of firefighters, supported by water-dropping helicopters, mounted an aggressive response on the ground and from the air. Two personnel were hospitalised with heat-related injuries, and Interstate 5, the principal artery between Orange County and San Diego, was closed in both directions for several hours.

By Saturday, crews had attained 25% containment, enabling officials to lift most evacuation orders, though one street in San Clemente remained restricted. The state also obtained a federal Fire Management Assistance Grant to offset eligible firefighting expenses.

The fire was one of several to erupt during a spell of acute fire danger; another blaze consumed more than 3,000 acres at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton. Investigators have yet to determine what sparked the Norte Fire.

A rapidly spreading wildfire on the Orange County coastline has once again highlighted Southern California's vulnerability to autumn fire seasons. The Norte Fire damaged or destroyed at least six homes and triggered evacuation orders for approximately 16,000 residents before firefighters brought it partially under control.

The fire broke out on Friday morning near San Clemente and moved swiftly towards San Juan Capistrano. Its rapid progress was attributable to a combination of factors: powerful Santa Ana winds blowing from inland areas towards the coast, abnormally high temperatures, low humidity and vegetation left extremely dry by the season. In total, about 570 acres were burned.

The emergency response was substantial. Hundreds of firefighters deployed ground crews and aircraft, and two of them required hospital treatment for heat-related injuries. Interstate 5, a vital transport corridor to San Diego, was temporarily closed, and shelters were established for displaced residents.

By Saturday, containment had reached 25%, and the majority of evacuation orders had been rescinded. California also secured federal assistance from FEMA to defray firefighting costs, an indication of the financial burden such incidents impose.

The Norte Fire coincided with several other blazes, including one exceeding 3,000 acres at Camp Pendleton. While its cause remains under investigation, the episode underscores how hot, dry and windy conditions can transform a small fire into a regional emergency within hours.

threat.ex: Pollution is a threat to wildlife.

through.ex: The shop is open Monday through Friday.

time.ex: For the first time, dentists will join.

to.en: towards; also used before a verb

tore.en: moved through very fast and with force
tore.ex: The storm tore through the town.

total.ex: The total cost was two million.

town.en: a place where people live, smaller than a city
town.ex: She grew up in a small town.

transform.ex: The new park will transform the area.

transport.en: systems for moving people or goods
transport.ex: Public transport here is cheap and fast.

treatment.en: medical care for an illness or injury
treatment.ex: He is receiving treatment for cancer.

under.en: according to a rule or agreement

underscores.en: shows clearly how important something is
underscores.ex: The report underscores the need for action.

example.en: The accident underscores the need for safer roads.
example.zh: 這起事故凸顯了更安全道路的必要性。

note.usage: 常見 underscore the need/importance of sth；同 underline。

noteEn.meaning: shows clearly that something is important.

noteHi.exampleTr: यह दुर्घटना सुरक्षित सड़कों की ज़रूरत को रेखांकित करती है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी बात के महत्व को उजागर करना।
noteHi.usage: underscore the need/importance; underline के समान।

noteEs.exampleTr: El accidente subraya la necesidad de carreteras más seguras.
noteEs.usage: Se usa underscore the need / importance.

noteJa.exampleTr: その事故は安全な道路の必要性を浮き彫りにする。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 사고는 더 안전한 도로의 필요성을 부각한다.

unseasonable.en: not usual for the time of year
unseasonable.ex: We had unseasonable snow in May.

unusually.ex: It was unusually hot for October.

upper.ex: Upper income groups pay more tax.

example.en: Dry vegetation can catch fire very easily.
example.zh: 乾燥的植被很容易起火。

note.usage: 不可數名詞；常與 dense/thick/dry 連用。

noteHi.exampleTr: सूखी वनस्पति बहुत आसानी से आग पकड़ लेती है।

noteEs.exampleTr: La vegetación seca puede arder con mucha facilidad.

noteJa.exampleTr: 乾燥した植生は非常に燃えやすい。

noteKo.exampleTr: 마른 초목은 아주 쉽게 불이 붙는다.

vulnerability.en: the state of being easily harmed
vulnerability.ex: The flood showed the town's vulnerability to storms.

example.en: The storm exposed the city's vulnerability to floods.
example.zh: 這場風暴暴露了該市易受洪水侵襲的弱點。

note.usage: 常見 vulnerability to sth；形容詞 vulnerable。

noteEn.meaning: the state of being easily harmed.

noteHi.exampleTr: तूफ़ान ने बाढ़ के प्रति शहर की असुरक्षा उजागर की।
noteHi.meaning: आसानी से नुकसान झेलने की स्थिति।

noteEs.exampleTr: La tormenta reveló la vulnerabilidad de la ciudad a las inundaciones.
noteEs.usage: Se usa vulnerability to algo; adjetivo vulnerable.

noteJa.exampleTr: 嵐は街の洪水に対する脆弱さを露わにした。

noteKo.exampleTr: 폭풍은 홍수에 대한 도시의 취약성을 드러냈다.

water.en: the clear liquid that falls as rain and that we drink

water-dropping.en: that drops water from the air on fires

wealthy.ex: They live in a wealthy area.

weather.ex: The weather in Ireland changes quickly.

week.ex: I go swimming twice a week.

weekend.ex: We go hiking at the weekend.

which.en: used to add information about a thing

wildfire.en: a large fire that spreads quickly over land
wildfire.ex: The wildfire burned for a week.

wind-driven.en: pushed or spread by the wind
wind-driven.ex: A wind-driven fire is hard to stop.

windy.ex: It was too windy to fly the drone.

worked.en: were successful; had the result wanted
worked.ex: The new idea worked very well.

yet.ex: The results are not out yet.
